summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The Magna Carta (the codified historical kernel) read strictly in its original context as a narrow set of baron-specific privileges versus read expansively in later centuries as the foundational mandate for universal due process and human rights. The exact same text is wielded to emit entirely different constraints on sovereign power.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The standardized medical taxonomy (a codified, authoritative text) read by institutional psychiatry as an objective mapping of biological pathology versus read by neurodiversity advocates as a socially constructed boundary enforcing normative behavior. A high-stakes epistemic contest that alters the beneficiary and victim sets of medical coercion.

human_readable: Ma'at as Cosmic and Political Order
summary: [SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The ancient Egyptian concept of Ma'at (a deep practice-norm and textual kernel) read by the Pharaoh as a divine mandate for absolute centralization and resource extraction versus read by local nomarchs/commoners as a reciprocal obligation requiring the ruler to provide justice and stability. An authority-grounding contest over the limits of a shared religious commitment.

[SPECULATIVE ESTIMATE] KERNEL CONTEST: The official Parker Brothers/Hasbro rulebook (the fixed text) read strictly as a fast, brutal demonstration of rent extraction (its original design intent) versus the proliferation of 'house rules' (Free Parking cash, no auctions) read as a necessary social scaffold to prolong coordination and reduce friction. A pristine micro-level commitment system where the text is constantly overridden by community practice.
